junction.name: Elliott Avenue West & West Harrison Street, Seattle

claims.text: Elliott Avenue West & West Harrison Street had 42 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 2 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $2.9 million a year (injury crashes only: deaths are not valued in this figure).
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.3 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $431,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 0.9 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $316,000 a year; check on site: the pavement's friction is low now (wet-road crashes alone do not show it).
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 4th Avenue West, Elliott Avenue West, West Harrison Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
